newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan army retakes town, villages - papers.
newsitem.headline: Sudan army retakes town, villages - papers.

text.p: Sudanese newspapers said on Tuesday government forces had recaptured a town from Eritrean forces and more than 20 villages from southern rebels.

"The armed forces and the popular defence have managed to liberate the town of Marasit, south of Tokar," Al-Sudan Al-Hadith quoted the Red Sea state's Minister of Social Affairs and Culture, Army Brigadier Mohamad Ali Abdalla, as saying.
"Our forces inflicted on the enemy Eritrean forces huge losses in lives and equipment and seized large quantities of arms and ammunition," it added.
The paper did not say when the army took the town back.

It said Tokar Commissioner Abdel Rahman Bilal and a number of officials had visited Marasit and the hilly areas surrounding it after "our forces had managed to chase the attacking Eritrean troops outside the area".

The rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) said earlier this month that rebels overran Marasit, 25 km (15 miles) from Tokar, on April 17 and pushed on towards Tokar 150 km (90 miles) southeast of Port Sudan.
The rebels have said their offensive in the northeast is aimed at cutting the road from Khartoum to Port Sudan on the Red Sea, Sudan's main commercial link with the outside world.
The Sudanese government has accused Eritrean, Ethiopian and Ugandan troops of taking part in rebel offensives in the south, east and northeast. The three countries deny the charges.
The private newspaper Alwan said the army and its volunteer militia Popular Defence Force had recaptured more than 20 villages in the Nuba area of southern Kordofan in central Sudan.

The daily said "the armed forces and...the Popular Defence Force achieved big victories in the theatre of operations recently and managed to recapture several areas around Kadugli, Dilling and Talodi and...the road from Talodi towards upper Nile has been opened officially".
The road had been closed for 13 years, the paper added in its report, which gave no source. It did not say when the operation took place. The two reports could not be independently confirmed.
